newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sends advisers to Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sends advisers to Kabila's Congo.

text.p: A South African government delegation leaves for Kinshasa on Tuesday to advise President Laurent Kabila on reconstruction of his country's fiscal infrastructure, a foreign affairs official said on Monday.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Pieter Swanepoel said Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad would lead the two-day mission to assess the financial problems facing Kabila's Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire.
"It's a follow-up on Deputy President (Thabo) Mbeki's meeting with Kabila in Lubumbashi last month and further talks between South Africa and the Congo in Harare recently.
"It's a response to a request from Mr Kabila's government for assistance," Swanepoel said.
Mbeki was the first high-ranking African leader to visit Kabila after he proclaimed himself president of the former Zaire, Africa's third-largest country.
Swanepoel said Pahad would be accompanied by officials from the central Reserve Bank, the Johannesburg-based Development Bank of Southern Africa and the departments of finance and trade and industry.
"At this point there is no participation by the private sector or the department of transport. This mission is about restoring the country's financial infrastructure," he said.

South Africa had been expected to invite mining industry representatives to join the delegation both to explore opportunities for South African companies and to offer advice on the revival of Congo's mining sector.
Kabila ousted former dictator Mobutu Sese Seko earlier this year after a seven-month campaign, but found the treasury looted and the government in virtual collapse.
